The story goes that she was the daughter of the Phoenician king Eschmunazar II and the goddess Tanit. When Eschmunazar II died, he was succeeded by his brother Hadad. Amarian was married to Hadad, but he soon became jealous of her beauty and attempted to kill her. She was saved by Baal and taken to the island of Cyprus, where she was revered as a goddess. The name 'Amarian' was later adopted by early Christian communities as a symbol of deliverance from persecution.

Amarian is particularly remembered for his 'Twenty-One Steps of Humility', a work that outlines the steps a Christian should take in order to grow in humility.
